tips.title: Choosing the Right Paint for Scale Models
tips.text: For scale models, acrylic paints are the most versatile and user-friendly. Vallejo Model Air and Model Color offer a wide range of colors suitable for both airbrush and brush application. For enamel-based paints like Tamiya Acrylic, use enamel thinners for cleaning and reduce paint viscosity with Tamiya Acrylic Thinner. Lacquers like Alclad II are ideal for clear coats and metal finishes, but require proper ventilation and slower drying times.

tips.title: Selecting the Right Sandpaper Grits for Model Building
tips.text: For plastic model kits, start with 240-grit sandpaper to remove mold seams and prepare surfaces for painting. Use 400-grit for smoothing filled gaps and blending transitions. Fine-tune details with 600-grit before applying decals. Finally, use 800-grit for a glass-smooth finish before applying clear coats. Always sand in one direction and avoid circular motions to prevent scratches.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Filler for Model Kit Gaps
tips.text: For small gaps and imperfections, use Vallejo Plastic Putty. Apply with a brush, let dry, then sand smooth with 400-grit sandpaper. For larger gaps, mix Tamiya Extra Thin Cement with baking soda to create a lightweight, gap-filling putty. Apply with a toothpick or brush, let dry, then sand smooth with 240-grit. Avoid using super glue alone, as it shrinks and leaves voids.

tips.title: Photo-Etch vs. Resin Detail Parts: Which to Choose?
tips.text: Photo-etch parts from brands like Eduard offer thin, delicate details with a realistic appearance. They're ideal for small, intricate details like antennae, ladders, and mesh. Resin detail parts, such as those from Clear Prop Models, provide larger, more robust details like engine blocks, wheels, and weapons. Choose based on the scale and type of detail you need. Both can be glued with CA glue or super glue.

tips.title: Selecting the Right Decal Setting Solutions
tips.text: For standard decals, use Microscale Micro Set to promote adhesion and reduce silvering. Apply Micro Set with a brush or eye dropper, let it soak in for a few seconds, then carefully place the decal. After drying, apply Micro Sol to melt away the decal carrier film, promoting a smooth, seamless finish. For complex decals, consider Arma Hobby's Decal Softener, which gently melts and reshapes decals for a better fit.
